guidelines.detail: refines FID-01 (The description identifies entering personal and payment information as a distinct action, while the reference has a corresponding activity with no counterpart in the generated model. This specializes FID-01 for distinct input actions; the flow records do not establish a separate general gateway guideline.)

refines FID-03 (The description says the generated ticket is sent to the customer, while the matched generated label says it is received; preserving the described action avoids this semantic change. This refines the documented guidance to use short, faithful labels by specifying which details to preserve.)

refines FLOW-01 (The cited records show missing flows from activities to gateways. This guideline addresses that missing transition without implying that a gateway should be added unless the description supports a decision or synchronization point.)

documentation rule FID-01 not applied (The description explicitly states selecting a route and providing payment details, but the records show no corresponding generated elements. These support modeling the stated actions as activities. I do not rely on M3: the description says the customer may receive communications, while the reference's “Send instructions” task does not clearly match that description; X4 also shows the generator rep)

same as LRN-016 (The description says the system sends the generated ticket to the customer, but the generated label says the customer receives it, changing the action’s perspective. This supports preserving the described meaning in element labels, which is already covered by learned guideline LRN-016.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant enters information or other inputs as a distinct action: Model that action as a separate activity in the appropriate sequence; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant enters information or other inputs as a distinct action

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states an activity or outcome and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient: label the corresponding BPMN element with concise wording that preserves those stated details and does not substitute a different action or meaning
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or outcome and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description places a decision or synchronization point after an activity: Connect the preceding activity to that gateway with a sequence flow in the same process scope; do not omit the transition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description places a decision or synchronization point after an activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states distinct actions that a participant performs before a later process step
